superseded_definition: Supratemporal fenestra: present, relatively large (0); almost closed or absent (1) (Wilson, 2002; Mannion et al., 2012).
retained_definition: Supratemporal fenestra: present (0); absent (1). 260
rationale: Both characters describe closure/presence of the supratemporal fenestra. The later formulation expands present/absent into relatively large versus almost closed/absent; the concepts never co-occur in the same analysed matrix.

superseded_definition: Radius, distal condyle orientation: perpen- dicular or bevelled less than 20° to long axis of shaft (0); bevelled at least 20° to long axis of shaft (1) (Curry Rogers & Forster, 2001; Wilson, 2002; Mannion et al., 2013; note that in most taxa only the lateral half of the distal end is bevelled, but this is used as the measure- ment in those instances).
retained_definition: Radius, distal condyle orientation: perpendicular to (0) or bevelled approximately 20° proximolat- erally (1) relative to long axis of shaft.
rationale: Both characters score orientation/bevelling of the distal radial condyle relative to the shaft. The later formulation formalizes an approximately 20° threshold; the concepts never co-occur in the same analysed matrix.

superseded_definition: Ulna, distal end: prominently expanded pos- teriorly (0); unexpanded (1) (D’Emic, 2012).
retained_definition: Ulna, distal end: expanded posteriorly (0); unex- panded (1).
rationale: Both characters score posterior expansion versus non-expansion of the distal ulna. The later definition adds 'prominently' but does not change the biological proposition; the concepts never co-occur in the same analysed matrix.

superseded_definition: Anterior caudal ribs, shape in anterior view: triangular, tapering distally (0); wing-like, with a dorsolaterally oriented dorsal margin (1) (Berman & McIntosh, 1978; McIntosh, 1990; Upchurch, 1995, 1998; Whitlock et al., 2011).
retained_definition: Anterior caudal transverse processes, shape: triangular, tapering distally (0); ‘wing-like’, not tapering distally (1).
rationale: Anterior caudal rib/transverse-process shape is the same triangular-versus-wing-like character.

superseded_definition: Ischium, shape of distal shaft in trans- verse cross-section: triangular, depth of ischial shaft increases medially (0); blade-like, medial and lat- eral depths subequal (1) (Wilson, 2002; polarity reversed here).
retained_definition: Ischial distal shaft, shape: triangular, depth of ischial shaft increases medially (0); bladelike, medial and lateral depths subequal (1).
rationale: Same distal ischial shaft cross-sectional morphology; M19/M26 reverse the state polarity.

superseded_definition: Subnarial foramen and anterior maxillary foramen, relative position: well distanced from one another (distance equals several subnarial foramen diameters) (0); separated by narrow bony isthmus (distance equals approximately one subnarial foramen diameter) (1) (Wilson, 2002; modified here).
retained_definition: Subnarial foramen and anterior maxillary fora- men, position: well distanced from one another (0); separated by narrow bony isthmus (1).
rationale: Same relative spacing of the subnarial and anterior maxillary foramina; M19/M26 quantify the distance.

superseded_definition: Middle caudal neural arches: situated over the mid-point of the centrum with approximately sube- qual amounts of the centrum exposed at either end (0); located on the anterior half of the centrum (1) (Calvo & Salgado, 1995; Upchurch, 1995, 1998; Salgado et al., 1997).
retained_definition: Anterior and middle caudal vertebrae, neural arches, location: over the midpoint of the centrum with approximately subequal amounts of the centrum exposed at either end (0), on the anterior half of the centrum (1). (Salgado et al., 1997; Upchurch et al., 2004.)
rationale: Same caudal neural-arch position over the centrum; M19/M26 restrict the character to middle caudals.

superseded_definition: Postorbital, posterior (squamosal) process: present as a distinct process (0); absent (1) (Wilson, 2002, 2005b).
retained_definition: Postorbital, posterior process: present (0); absent (1).
rationale: Same postorbital posterior-process presence/absence character.

superseded_definition: Anterior caudal neural spines, SPRL: ab- sent, or restricted to the anterolateral margin of the spine (0); present, extending onto lateral aspect of neural spine (1) (Wilson, 2002; Mannion et al., 2012; modified here).
retained_definition: Anterior caudal neural arches, spinoprezygapo- physeal lamina (sprl): absent (0); present and extending onto lateral aspect of neural spine (1).
rationale: Same anterior-caudal SPRL extension onto the lateral neural-spine surface.

superseded_definition: Humeral distal condyles, articular surface: flat anteroposteriorly and restricted to distal portion of humerus (0); anteroposteriorly convex so that it curves up onto the anterior and posterior faces of the humerus (1) (Wilson, 2002; Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Humeral distal condyles, articular surface shape: restricted to distal portion of humerus (0); exposed on anterior portion of humeral shaft (1).
rationale: Same humeral distal-condyle articular-surface exposure/convexity character.

superseded_definition: Tooth crowns, longitudinal groove parallel- ing mesial and distal margins on the labial surface: labial grooves present (0); absent (1) (Upchurch, 1995; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Prominent grooves near mesial and distal margins of labial surface of tooth crowns (U86) / absent present
rationale: Same labial tooth-crown grooves near the mesial and distal margins, with reversed polarity.

superseded_definition: Infratemporal (or laterotemporal) fenestra, anterior extension: reaching midpoint of orbit (0); reaching or surpassing anterior margin of orbit (1) (Upchurch, 1995, 1998; Ksepka & Norell, 2010; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Laterotemporal fenestra, anterior extension: posterior to orbit (0); ventral to orbit (1).
rationale: Same anterior extent of the infratemporal/laterotemporal fenestra relative to the orbit.

superseded_definition: Pubis, development of ambiens process: absent or small and confluent with anterior margin of pubis (0); prominent, projecting anteriorly (1) (McIntosh, 1990; Upchurch, 1998; modified here).
retained_definition: Pubis, ambiens process development: small, con- fluent with (0) or prominent, projecting anteri- orly from (1) anterior margin of pubis.
rationale: Same development of the pubic ambiens process.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior dorsal neural spines, spi- nopostzygapophyseal lamina (SPOL) shape: single (0); divided into medial and lateral branches (1) (Wilson, 1999, 2002).
retained_definition: Middle and posterior dorsal neural arches spino- postzygapophyseal lamina (spol) shape: single (0); divided (1).
rationale: Same single-versus-divided spinopostzygapophyseal lamina in middle/posterior dorsals.

superseded_definition: Anterior caudal neural spines, spinoprezyga- pophyseal lamina (SPRL)–spinopostzygapophyseal lamina (SPOL) contact: absent (0); present, forming a prominent lateral lamina on the neural spine (1) (Wilson, 1999, 2002; revised here so that only taxa in which the SPRL extends onto the lateral surface are scored).
retained_definition: Anterior caudal neural arches, spinoprezygapo- physeal lamina (sprl)-spinopostzygapophyseal lamina (spol) contact: absent (0); present, form- ing a prominent lamina on lateral aspect of neu- ral spine (1).
rationale: Same SPRL-SPOL contact forming a lateral lamina on anterior caudal neural spines.

superseded_definition: Ischium to pubis proximodistal length ratio: greater than 0.8 (0); 0.80 or less (1) (Calvo & Salgado, 1995; Salgado et al., 1997; Upchurch, 1998; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Ischium/pubis length ratio (Salgado et al., 1997, modi-fied): 1.20 (0); between 1.20 and 0.80 (1); 0.80 (2).
rationale: Same ischium:pubis proximodistal length-ratio variable with a simplified state scheme.

superseded_definition: Anterior–middle chevrons, articular facet sur- face: flat or anteroposteriorly convex (0); divided into anterior and posterior facets by a furrow (1) (Powell, 1987, 2003; Santucci & Arruda-Campos, 2011; D’Emic, 2012).
retained_definition: Anterior and middle chevrons, articular facets: contiguous (0); each facet divided into an anterior and posterior section, separated by a furrow (1).
rationale: Same division of anterior/middle chevron articular facets by a furrow.

superseded_definition: Teeth, number of replacement teeth per al- veolus: three or fewer (0); four or more (1) (Wilson, 2002).
retained_definition: Replacement teeth per alveolus, number: two or fewer (0); more than four (1).
rationale: Same number of replacement teeth per alveolus; state thresholds differ.

superseded_definition: Metatarsals, distal end orientation of meta- tarsal IV: perpendicular to long axis of bone (0); bev- elled to face medially (1) (D’Emic, 2012).
retained_definition: Metatarsal IV, distal end, orientation: roughly perpendicular to long axis of bone (0); bevelled upwards medially (1).
rationale: Same distal metatarsal-IV orientation/bevelling character.

superseded_definition: Metacarpals, metacarpal I to metacarpal IV proximodistal length ratio: less than 1.0 (0); 1.0 or greater (1) (Wilson & Sereno, 1998).
retained_definition: Metacarpal I, length: shorter than (0) or longer than (1) metacarpal IV.
rationale: Same metacarpal-I:metacarpal-IV proximodistal length relationship.

superseded_definition: Dentary, depth of anterior end: maintains dorsoventral height anteriorly, or increases only slightly (i.e. ratio of height of dentary at anterior end to height of dentary at midlength is 1.2 or lower) (0); increases in dorsoventral height anteriorly (i.e. ratio of height of dentary at anterior end to height of dentary at midlength is higher than 1.2) (1) (Upchurch, 1998; Wilson & Sereno, 1998; Wilson, 2002; modified here).
retained_definition: Dentary, depth of anterior end of ramus: slightly less than that of dentary at midlength (0); 150% minimum depth (1).
rationale: Same anterior deepening of the dentary; M19/M26 quantify the ratio.

superseded_definition: Basipterygoid processes, orientation in lat- eral view: directed 80° or more to skull roof (normally perpendicular) (0); angled less than 80° to skull roof (anteroventrally directed) (1) (McIntosh, 1990; Wilson, 2002; Whitlock, 2011a; Mannion et al., 2012; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Basipterygoid processes, orientation: perpendic- ular to (0) or angled approximately 45° to (1) skull roof.
rationale: Same basipterygoid-process orientation relative to the skull roof, with an expanded angular state scheme.

superseded_definition: Ischium, morphology of conjoined distal ends: ‘V’-shaped, forming an angle of 90° or less (usually ap- proximately 50°) with each other (0); forming an angle of more than 90° (typically flat, nearly coplanar) (1) (Upchurch, 1998; Wilson & Sereno, 1998).
retained_definition: Ischial distal shafts, cross-sectional shape: V- shaped, forming an angle of nearly 50° with each other (0); flat, nearly coplanar (1).
rationale: Same V-shaped versus nearly coplanar conjoined distal ischia.

superseded_definition: Scapular blade, orientation of blade long-axis with respect to coracoid articulation: more than 70° (usually approximately perpendicular) (0); 70° or less (1) (Wilson, 2002; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Scapular blade, orientation: perpendicular to (0) or forming a 45° angle with (1) coracoid articulation.
rationale: Same scapular-blade long-axis orientation relative to the coracoid articulation.

superseded_definition: Jugal, contact with ectopterygoid: present (0); absent, ectopterygoid contacts maxilla instead (1) (Upchurch, 1995).
retained_definition: Jugal-ectopterygoid contact: present (0); absent (1).
rationale: Same jugal-ectopterygoid contact presence/absence character.

superseded_definition: Femoral distal condyles, orientation relative to long axis of femoral shaft: bevelled dorsolaterally approximately 10° (tibial condyle extends further dis- tally than fibular condyle) (0); perpendicular (tibial and fibular condyles extend approximately the same distance distally) (1); bevelled dorsomedially approxi- mately 10° (fibular condyle extends further distally than tibial condyle) (2) (Wilson, 2002; Mannion et al., 2013) [ordered].
retained_definition: Femoral distal condyles, orientation: perpendic- ular or slightly bevelled dorsolaterally (0) or bevelled dorsomedially approximately 10° (1) relative to femoral shaft.
rationale: Same distal femoral-condyle orientation relative to the shaft, with the intermediate perpendicular state separated.

superseded_definition: Basal tubera, relative prominence: antero- posterior width is approximately 33%, or more, of dorsoventral height of the tubera (such tubera are distinct projections from the basipterygoid) (0); sheet- like, anteroposterior width is less than 33% (normally around 20%) of the dorsoventral height of the tubera (such tubera are reduced to slight swellings on the ventral surface of the basipterygoid) (1) (Wilson, 2002; Whitlock, 2011a; modified here).
retained_definition: Basal tubera, anteroposterior depth: approxi- mately half dorsoventral height (0); sheet-like, 20% dorsoventral height (1).
rationale: Same sheet-like versus prominent basal-tubera anteroposterior depth character.

superseded_definition: Metacarpals, longest metacarpal to radius proximodistal length ratio: less than 0.40 (0); 0.40 or greater (1) (McIntosh, 1990; Calvo & Salgado, 1995; Upchurch, 1998; Wilson & Sereno, 1998; Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Longest metacarpal-to-radius ratio: close to 0.3 (0); 0.45 or more (1).
rationale: Same longest-metacarpal:radius length ratio; the 0.40 threshold closely reformulates the older ratio character.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior dorsal neural spines: taper- ing or not flaring distally (0); flared distally with tri- angular aliform processes projecting laterally from the top [formed primarily from the expansion of the spi- nopostzygapophyseal laminae (SPOLs)] (1) (Upchurch, 1998; Wilson & Sereno, 1998; Wilson, 2002; Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Middle and posterior dorsal neural spines, shape: tapering or not flaring distally (0); flared distally, with pendant, triangular lateral pro- cesses (1).
rationale: Same distally flared middle/posterior dorsal neural spine with triangular aliform processes.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior cervical neural arches, centroprezygapophyseal lamina (CPRL): single (0); bifurcates into medial and lateral branches that both contact the prezygapophysis (1) (Upchurch, 1995, 1998; Wilson, 2002; Whitlock 2011a; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Middle and posterior cervical neural arches, cen- troprezygapophyseal lamina (cprl), shape: single (0); divided (1). Wilson [1999a: 650, 651] errone- ously lists this as characterizing dorsal neural arches.)
rationale: Same single-versus-divided centroprezygapophyseal lamina in middle/posterior cervicals.

superseded_definition: Frontal, contribution to margin of supratem- poral fenestra: present (0); absent, frontal excluded from anterior margin of fenestra by a postorbital-pari- etal contact (1) (Wilson & Sereno, 1998).
retained_definition: Frontal contribution to supratemporal fossa: present (0); absent (1).
rationale: Same frontal contribution to the supratemporal fenestra/fossa margin.

superseded_definition: Astragalus, mediolateral width to maximum proximodistal height ratio: 1.8 or greater (0); less than 1.8 (1) (Wilson, 2002; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Astragalus, transverse length: 50% more than (0) or subequal to (1) proximodistal height.
rationale: Same astragalar transverse-width:proximodistal-height ratio.

superseded_definition: Ischium, symphysis between the ischia: termi- nates at the base of the proximal plates (emarginate distal to pubic articulation) (0); extends along the ven- tral edges of the proximal plates as well as the distal shafts, so that there is no V-shaped gap between the anterior ends of the ischia in dorsal view (no emargin- ation distal to pubic articulation) (1) (McIntosh, 1990; Upchurch, 1998; Wilson, 2002).
retained_definition: Ischial blade, shape: emarginate distal to pubic peduncle (0); no emargination distal to pubic peduncle (1). 264
rationale: Same emargination/no-emargination of the ischial symphysis distal to the pubic articulation.

superseded_definition: Tooth serrations/denticles: present (0); ab- sent (1) (Wilson, 2002; Upchurch et al., 2004; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Marginal tooth denticles: present (0); absent on posterior edge (1); absent on both anterior and posterior edges (2).
rationale: Same marginal tooth denticle/serration character; M19/M26 collapse the edge-specific states to present/absent.

superseded_definition: Sternal plate, shape in dorsal view: subcir- cular or oval (0); triangular (created by an acute an- terolateral projection) (1); elliptical with a mildly or strongly concave lateral margin (2) (Calvo & Salgado, 1995; Upchurch, 1998; Wilson, 2002; Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Sternal plate, shape: oval (0); crescentic (1).
rationale: Same overall sternal-plate outline; M19/M26 expand the shape states.

superseded_definition: Scapular glenoid surface, orientation: faces anteroventrally and/or slightly laterally (0); deflected to face anteroventrally and medially (1) (Wilson & Sereno, 1998; Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Scapular glenoid, orientation: relatively flat or laterally facing (0); strongly bevelled medially (1).
rationale: Same scapular glenoid orientation, especially medial beveling.

superseded_definition: Postorbital, ventral process: anteroposterior and mediolateral diameters equal, or mediolater- ally compressed (0); anteroposteriorly compressed (1) (Wilson & Sereno, 1998; Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Postorbital, ventral process shape: transversely narrow (0); broader transversely than anteropos- teriorly (1).
rationale: Same transverse-versus-anteroposterior proportions of the postorbital ventral process.

superseded_definition: Frontal, anteroposterior length to transverse width ratio: 1.0 or greater (0); less than 1.0 and >0.5 (1); 0.5 or less (2) (Whitlock, 2011a; Tschopp & Mateus, 2013; Poropat et al., 2016; revised here to add an extra state) [ordered].
retained_definition: Frontal, anteroposterior length: approximately twice (0) or less than (1) minimum transverse breadth.
rationale: Same frontal anteroposterior-length:transverse-width variable with an added intermediate state.

superseded_definition: Lateral temporal fenestra, shape in lateral view: taller than wide anteroposteriorly and subtrian- gular (anteroposteriorly broader ventral margin and narrower dorsal apex) (0); linear, slit-like, crescentic (longer anteroposteriorly than high dorsoventrally) (1) (Harris, 2006b; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Morphology of infratemporal fenestra (C9, S6) / subrectangular subtriangular 'linear (slit-like, crescentic)'
rationale: C12 C34 and M19/M26 score the shape of the lateral/infratemporal fenestra; the later formulation collapses the subrectangular state.

superseded_definition: Quadratojugal, angle between anterior and dorsal processes in lateral view: less than or equal to 90°, so that the quadrate shaft is directed dorsally (0); greater than 90° (usually approaching 130°), so that the quadrate shaft slants posterodorsally (1) (Gauthier, 1986; Upchurch, 1995).
retained_definition: Angle between rostral and dorsal processes of the quadratojugal (U27) / roughly_90º '>>90º'
rationale: Both score the angle between the anterior/rostral and dorsal processes of the quadratojugal; the later wording explicitly links the angle to quadrate-shaft orientation.

superseded_definition: Dorsal centra, lateral pneumatic foramina: have margins which are flush with the lateral surface of the centrum (0); are set within a lateral fossa on the lateral surface of the centrum (1) (Bonaparte & Coria, 1993; Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Lateral position of pleurocoelous foramina on thoracic vertebral bodies (U130) / absent 'flush with lateral surface (no pleurocoelous fossa)' set_within_pleurocoelous_fossa
rationale: Both score whether dorsal/thoracic pneumatic foramina are flush with the centrum surface or set within a lateral fossa; C12 also includes an absent state.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior dorsal neural spines, an- terior spinodiapophyseal lamina (aSPDL): absent (0); present (1) (Upchurch et al., 2004; Poropat et al., 2016; note that the presence of an aSPDL can only be con- firmed when a pSPDL is also present).
retained_definition: Accessory spinodiapophyseal lamina on thoracic vertebrae with non-bifid spinous processes (U151) / absent present
rationale: C12's accessory spinodiapophyseal lamina is the anterior SPDL/aSPDL subsequently formalized in the M19/M26 wording.

superseded_definition: Sacrum, ratio of mediolateral width across sa- cral vertebrae and ribs (taken at midlength on the co- ossified sacrum) to average length of a sacral centrum: less than 4.0 (0); 4.0 or higher (1) (Upchurch, 1998).
retained_definition: Ratio of maximum mediolateral width across sacral vertebrae and ribs:average length of sacral vertebral body (U164) / '<4.0' '>=4.0'
rationale: Definition is effectively identical: sacral mediolateral width across ribs divided by average sacral centrum length, threshold 4.0.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior dorsal centra, posterior ar- ticular face mediolateral width to dorsoventral height ratio: less than 1.0 (0); 1.0 or greater (1) (Upchurch, 1998; Upchurch et al., 2004; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Cross-sectional morphology of caudal thoracic vertebral bodies (U131) / subcircular dorsoventrally_compressed
rationale: Both score transverse-versus-dorsoventral proportions of posterior/caudal dorsal centra; M19/M26 express the C12 subcircular-versus-compressed condition as a width:height ratio.

superseded_definition: Anterior caudal centra, mediolateral width to dorsoventral height (excluding chevron facets) of an- terior surface ratio: less than 1.0 (0); 1.0 or greater (1) (Upchurch et al., 2004; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Morphology of articular surfaces in proximal caudal vertebral bodies (U172) / subcircular dorsoventrally_compressed mediolaterally_compressed
rationale: Both score mediolateral-versus-dorsoventral proportions of the anterior/proximal caudal articular surface; the later binary ratio collapses C12's three shape states.

superseded_definition: Scapular acromion (proximal plate), area situ- ated posterior to the acromial ridge: flat or convex (0); forms a separate excavated area (1) (Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Morphology of portion of acromion caudal to deltoid crest (U202) / flat_or_convex_and_decreases_in_mediolateral_thickness_toward_caudal_margin forms_distinct_fossa
rationale: Both score whether the scapular acromial area posterior to the deltoid/acromial ridge is flat/convex or forms a distinct fossa.

superseded_definition: Scapular blade, ridge on medial surface, close to junction with acromial plate and near dorsal margin: absent (0); present (1) (Sanz et al., 1999; Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Dorsal ridge on medial surface of scapular body (U204) / absent present
rationale: Both score a dorsal-positioned ridge on the medial surface of the scapular blade.

superseded_definition: Coracoid, dorsal margin in lateral view: lies below the level of the scapular acromion plate (sepa- rated from the latter by a V-shaped notch) (0); reaches or surpasses the level of the dorsal margin of the scapular acromion plate (1) (Upchurch, 1995, 1998; Upchurch et al., 2004; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Position of dorsal margin of coracoid with respect to dorsal margin of scapula (U207) / equal_or_dorsal_to_acromion 'ventral to acromion and separated from it by V-shaped notch'
rationale: Same position of the coracoid dorsal margin relative to the scapular acromion; state polarity is reversed.

superseded_definition: Humerus, proximal margin in anterior/pos- terior view: straight or convex (0); sinuous, as a re- sult of a prominently developed process (attachment site for M. supracoracoideus) on the lateral margin of the proximal end (1) (Upchurch, 1998; González Riga, 2003; González Riga et al., 2009; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Supracoracoideus tuberculum on proximolateral portion of humerus (U217) / absent present
rationale: Both score development of the proximolateral humeral process/tuberculum for M. supracoracoideus; M19/M26 operationalize it through proximal-margin sinuosity.

superseded_definition: Humeral deltopectoral crest, projection: anteriorly or anterolaterally (0); anteromedially, extending across the anterior face of the humerus (1) (Mannion et al., 2013; Upchurch et al., 2015; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Position of deltopectoral crest (U220) / restricted_to_lateral_edge_of_humerus expanded_medially_across_cranial_face_of_humerus
rationale: Same medial expansion/projection of the humeral deltopectoral crest across the anterior face.

superseded_definition: Humerus, distal-most part of the posterior surface (supracondylar fossa) is: flat or shallowly con- cave (0); deeply concave between prominent lateral and medial vertical condylar ridges (1) (Upchurch et al., 2004).
retained_definition: Distocaudal surface of humerus (U221) / shallowly_concave 'deeply concave, bounded between prominent vertical ridges'
rationale: Same distal posterior humeral/supracondylar-fossa depth character: shallow/flat versus deeply concave between condylar ridges.

superseded_definition: Ulna, articular surface of anteromedial pro- cess is: flat (0); concave along its length (1) (Upchurch, 1995, 1998).
retained_definition: Morphology of articular surface of craniomedial process of ulna in cranial view (U224) / flat strongly_concave_on_proximal_surface
rationale: Same flat-versus-concave articular surface of the ulnar anteromedial/craniomedial process.

superseded_definition: Manual ungual on digit I to metacarpal I proxi- modistal length ratio: 0.5 or greater (0); less than 0.5 (1) [Upchurch et al., 2004; Mannion et al., 2013; revised here so that taxa that have lost their manual phalan- ges (derived state for C242) are scored as a ‘?’].
retained_definition: Size of ungual on manual digit I (U240) / 'large (at least 50% length of metacarpal I)' 'reduced (<25% length of metacarpal I) or absent'
rationale: Same manual digit-I ungual length relative to metacarpal I; the later binary character collapses the strongly reduced/absent condition.

superseded_definition: Femur, femoral head, projection: directed medially (0); directed dorsomedially (1) (Upchurch et al., 2004; Curry Rogers, 2005; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Orientation of femoral caput in cranial view (U263) / medial_or_ventromedial dorsomedial
rationale: Same femoral-head/caput projection in anterior/cranial view: medial versus dorsomedial.

superseded_definition: Astragalus, in dorsal (or proximal) view: rect- angular, with anteroposterior lengths of medial and lateral margins subequal (or medial margin greater) (0); wedge-shaped, narrowing anteroposteriorly to- wards its medial end, such that it has a reduced anter- omedial corner (1) (Cooper, 1981; Upchurch, 1995, 1998; Wilson & Sereno, 1998).
retained_definition: Craniocaudal dimension of astragalus as seen in dorsal view (U285) / widens_medially narrows_medially
rationale: Same astragalar dorsal-view shape: approximately rectangular versus narrowing anteroposteriorly toward the medial side.

superseded_definition: Metatarsals I–III, rugosities on dorsolat- eral margins near distal ends: absent (0); present (1) (Upchurch, 1995).
retained_definition: Rugosities on distal parts of dorsolateral portions of bodies of metatarsals I-III (U294) / absent present
rationale: Same distal dorsolateral rugosities on metatarsals I–III, absent versus present.

superseded_definition: Pedal phalanx I-1, proximal and ventral sur- faces: meet at approximately 90° (0); proximoventral corner drawn out into thin plate underlying meta- tarsal I (1) (McIntosh et al., 1992).
retained_definition: Relationship of plantar to proximal surface of pedal phalanx I-1 (U301) / meet_at_~90°_angle 'meet at acute angle (area drawn into thin plate that projects caudal to distal condyles of metatarsal I)'
rationale: Same relationship of the proximal and plantar/ventral surfaces of pedal phalanx I-1, including the thin proximoventral plate.

superseded_definition: Scapula, acromial ridge: absent, or only very weakly developed (0); present and well-developed, so that a clear ridge is present and defines the posterior margin of a distinct fossa on the lateral surface of the acromion (1) (Upchurch, 1995; modified here).
retained_definition: Deltoid crest (= crest of acromion process) (U201) / absent present
rationale: C12 scores the deltoid/acromial crest as absent/present; M19/M26 score the same acromial ridge as weak/absent versus well developed.

superseded_definition: Middle caudal vertebrae, neural spines, orienta- tion: upright or lean posteriorly (0); lean anteri- orly (1). (Modified from Rose, 2007.)
retained_definition: Middle caudal neural spines, orientation: angled posterodorsally (0); vertical (1).
rationale: Both score orientation of middle-caudal neural spines. Wilson MC0133 distinguishes posterodorsal versus vertical, whereas DE12 collapses those into one state and adds an anteriorly leaning state; the underlying variable is the same.

superseded_definition: Cervical neural arches (post-Cv3), epipophy- ses: do not extend beyond the posterior margin of the postzygapophyses (0); extend beyond the posterior margin of the postzygapophyses (usually as prongs) (1) (Sereno et al., 1993; Yates, 2007; D’Emic, 2012; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Cervical vertebrae, epipophyses, shape: stout, pillar-like expansions above postzygapophyses (0); posteriorly projecting prongs (1).
rationale: M19/M26 explicitly cite D'Emic (2012) and operationalize the same epiphyseal shape/extension variable as projecting posterior prongs versus stout/non-projecting epipophyses.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior cervical neural arches, intra- postzygapophyseal lamina (TPOL) projects beyond the posterior margin of the neural arch [including the centropostzygapophyseal laminae (CPOL)], forming a prominent subrectangular projection in lateral view: absent (0); present (1) (D’Emic, 2012; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Cervical vertebrae, intrapostzygapophyseal lamina, shape: has little or no relief past margin of centropostzygapophyseal lamina (cpol) when viewed laterally (0); projects beyond cpol in lateral view, with distinct ‘kink’ (1).
rationale: M19/M26 explicitly cite D'Emic (2012) and score the same intrapostzygapophyseal lamina projecting beyond the CPOL/posterior neural-arch margin.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior cervical centra, parapophy- ses, dorsal surfaces: face dorsally or slightly dorso- laterally (0); deflected to face strongly dorsolaterally, such that the cervical ribs are displaced ventrally at least the same height as the centrum (1) (Wilson & Upchurch, 2009; D’Emic, 2012; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Cervical vertebrae, parapophyses, shape and ori- entation: weakly developed, project laterally or slightly ventrally from the centrum (0); broad and project ventrally such that cervical ribs are displaced ventrally more than the height of the centrum (1). (Modified from Wilson & Upchurch, 2009.)
rationale: Both score middle-posterior cervical parapophyseal orientation and the associated ventral displacement of cervical ribs; M19/M26 explicitly cite D'Emic (2012).

superseded_definition: Posteriormost cervical and anteriormost dorsal neural spines, shape in anterior/posterior view: taper dorsally, or mediolateral width remains con- stant along length (0); expand dorsally, with a strongly convex dorsal margin (‘paddle-shaped’) (1) (González Riga, 2005; D’Emic, 2012; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Anterior dorsal vertebrae, neural spines, shape: taper along their length (0), expand distally and end in a rounded, anteroposteriorly thin blade (‘paddle-shaped’) (1).
rationale: Same paddle-shaped dorsally expanded neural-spine morphology; M19/M26 explicitly cite D'Emic (2012) and extend the scope to the posteriormost cervical/anterior dorsal transition.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior dorsal centra, ventral keel: absent (0); present (1) (Mannion et al., 2012; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Middle and posterior dorsal vertebral centra, keel: absent (0); present (1).
rationale: Same presence/absence of a ventral keel on middle-posterior dorsal centra; later matrices formalize the serial position more explicitly.

superseded_definition: Humerus, anterior surface of distal lateral condyle: divided by a notch, forming two ridges (0); un- divided (1) (D’Emic, 2012).
retained_definition: Humerus, radial and ulnar condyles, shape: radial condyle divided on anterior face by a notch (0); undivided (1).
rationale: Definition-level match: the anterior surface of the distal lateral/radial humeral condyle is divided by a notch into two ridges versus undivided; M19/M26 cite D'Emic (2012).

superseded_definition: Metacarpals, metacarpal V, ratio of proximal end long-axis diameter to that of metacarpal I: less than 1.0 (0); 1.0 or greater (1) (D’Emic, 2012; Poropat et al., 2016).
retained_definition: Metacarpal V, proximal end, size: much smaller than proximal end of metacarpal I (0); sub- equal to or larger than proximal end of metacar- pal I (1).
rationale: Same metacarpal-V proximal-end size relative to metacarpal I. DE12 uses qualitative smaller versus subequal/larger states; M19/M26 express the same relation as a V:I ratio.

superseded_definition: Metacarpals, distal articular surfaces: ex- tend onto dorsal/anterior surface of metacarpal (0); restricted to distal surface (except sometimes in meta- carpal IV) (1) (Salgado et al., 1997; D’Emic, 2012).
retained_definition: Metacarpals, distal articular facets, shape: present and extend well onto external/ anterior face of bone (0); reduced almost entirely to distal face of the bone except in metatarsal IV (1). (Modified from Wilson, 2002.)
rationale: Same extent of metacarpal distal articular surfaces onto the dorsal/anterior face versus restriction to the distal face; M19/M26 cite D'Emic (2012).

superseded_definition: Ilium, pubic peduncle (measured at the ar- ticular surface), anteroposterior to mediolateral width ratio: greater than 0.5 (0); 0.5 or less (1) (Taylor, 2009; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Ilium, pubic peduncle, shape: anteroposterior and transverse dimensions subequal (0); trans- verse dimension more than 1.5 times anteropos- terior dimension (1).
rationale: Same anteroposterior:mediolateral proportions of the iliac pubic peduncle; later matrices use a numeric ratio threshold.

superseded_definition: Ischium, acetabular margin, in lateral view: flat or mildly concave (0); strongly concave, such that the pubic articular surface forms an anterodorsal pro- jection (1) (D’Emic, 2012; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Ischium, acetabular margin, shape: margin forms short, obtuse angle (0); margin strongly embayed, forming acute angle with tall iliac peduncle (1).
rationale: Same ischial acetabular-margin concavity/embayment; M19/M26 explicitly cite D'Emic (2012).

superseded_definition: Femur, proximodistally elongate midline ridge (linea intermuscularis cranialis) on anterior face, extending along most of shaft length: absent (0); pre- sent (1) (Otero, 2010; D’Emic, 2012).
retained_definition: Femur, longitudinal ridge on anterior face: absent (0); present (1). (Otero, 2010.)
rationale: Same longitudinal anterior femoral ridge (linea intermuscularis cranialis), absent versus present; M19/M26 cite Otero (2010) and D'Emic (2012).

superseded_definition: Fibula, proximal end with anteromedialy directed crest extending into a notch behind the cne- mial crest of the tibia: absent (0); present (1) (Wilson & Upchurch, 2009; D’Emic, 2012; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Fibula, proximal end, anterior crest: absent or poorly developed (0); well developed, creat- ing interlocking proximal crus (1). (Modified from Royo-Torres, 2009; Wilson & Upchurch, 2009.)
rationale: Same proximal fibular anterior/anteromedial crest that interlocks behind the tibial cnemial crest; M19/M26 cite Wilson & Upchurch (2009) and D'Emic (2012).

superseded_definition: Fibula, shaft in lateral view: straight (0); sig- moidal (1) (Canudo et al., 2008; Royo-Torres, 2009).
retained_definition: Fibula, shaft, shape: straight (0); sigmoid, such that proximal and distal faces are angled relative to midshaft (1). (Royo-Torres, 2009.)
rationale: Same fibular shaft shape in lateral view: straight versus sigmoidal.

superseded_definition: Metatarsals, medial surface of the proximal portion of metatarsal IV concave (for reception of metatarsal III): absent (0); present (1) (D’Emic et al., 2011; D’Emic, 2012).
retained_definition: Metatarsal IV, proximomedial end, shape: flat or slightly convex (0); possesses a distinct embay- ment (1).
rationale: Same proximomedial metatarsal-IV concavity/embayment for reception of metatarsal III; M19/M26 cite D'Emic et al. (2011) and D'Emic (2012).

superseded_definition: Tooth crowns, shape in labial view: spatulate or ‘spoon’-like (i.e. constricted at the base relative to midheight of the crown) (0); parallel-sided (i.e. little expansion above the root) (1) (Calvo, 1994; Upchurch, 1998).
retained_definition: Tooth shape: spoon-like (0); compressed cone chisel-like (1); pen- cil chisel-like (2) (modified from Calvo 1994 by Calvo and Gon- zález Riga 2003).
rationale: Both descend from the Calvo tooth-crown shape lineage. GA11 separates spoon-like, compressed chisel-like and pencil chisel-like states; M19/M26 collapse the non-spatulate conditions.

superseded_definition: Posterior cervical neural spines, dorsal half laterally expanded as a result of expansion of the lateral lamina (spinodiapophyseal lamina?): absent (0); present (1) (González Riga, 2005; González Riga et al., 2009, 2018; Gallina, 2011; González Riga & Ortiz David, 2014).
retained_definition: Posterior cervical neural spines lateraly expanded and wider than the centra: absent (0); present (1) (González Riga 2005).
rationale: Same posterior-cervical neural-spine lateral expansion described by González Riga (2005); M19/M26 explicitly cite Gallina (2011) among the lineage sources.

superseded_definition: Posterior cervical neural arches, spinodiapo- physeal fossa, at base of lateral surface of neural spine: absent or shallow fossa (0); deep fossa (1) (González Riga, 2005; González Riga et al., 2009, 2018).
retained_definition: Supradiapophyseal fossa in posterior cervical vertebrae: absent (0); shallow or reduced (1); deep and extended (2) (González Riga 2005).
rationale: Same posterior-cervical spinodiapophyseal/supradiapophyseal fossa depth variable; GA11 has absent, shallow and deep states whereas M19/M26 collapse absent+shallow.

superseded_definition: Anterior dorsal neural spines, orientation of anterior margin in lateral view: inclined anteriorly or vertical (0); posterodorsally inclined (1) (Upchurch et al., 2004; Mannion et al., 2013; revised here to clarify character statement).
retained_definition: Anterior dorsal neural spines inclined posteriorly more than 20 de- gree from vertical: absent (0); present (1) (modified from Wilson and Sereno 1998).
rationale: Same anterior-dorsal neural-spine inclination variable. GA11 uses a >20° posterior-inclination threshold; M19/M26 contrast anterior/vertical with posterodorsally inclined.

superseded_definition: Middle–posterior caudal neural arches, distance that prezygapophyses extend beyond the anterior margin of the centrum: less than 20% of cen- trum length (excluding ball), short prezygapophyses (0); 20% or greater of centrum length (excluding ball), elongate prezygapophyses (1) (González Riga, 2003; Mannion et al., 2013; note that in taxa without anteri- orly biased neural arches this prezygapophyseal ex- tension is extrapolated as if the arch was anteriorly positioned on the centrum).
retained_definition: Length proportions of prezygapophyses with respect to the centrum length in middle caudal vertebrae: shorter than 50% (0); between 40 to 50% (1); longer than 50% (2) (modified from González Riga 2003).
rationale: Same relative length of middle-caudal prezygapophyses from the González Riga (2003) lineage; later matrices use a lower 20% threshold and extend the scope into posterior caudals.

superseded_definition: Humerus, maximum mediolateral width of proximal end divided by proximodistal length: 0.4 or greater (0); less than 0.4 (1) (Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Humerus, breadth of proximal end with respect to the total length: less (0); or more (1) than the 50% (González Riga 2003).
rationale: Same maximum proximal humeral breadth divided by humeral length; GA11 uses 0.50 and M19/M26 use 0.40.

superseded_definition: Sternal plate, shape of posterior margin in dorsal/ventral view: convex (0); straight (1) (González Riga, 2003; González Riga et al., 2009).
retained_definition: Semilunar sternal plate with straight posterior border: absent (0); present (1) (González Riga 2003).
rationale: Same González Riga sternal-plate posterior-margin character: straight versus non-straight/convex.

superseded_definition: Ilium, preacetabular process orientation: lies in an approximately vertical plane (0); turns laterally towards its ventral tip to form a horizontal portion (1) (McIntosh, 1990; Powell, 1992; Upchurch, 1995, 1998).
retained_definition: Orientation of preacetabular lobe of ilium: nearly vertical (0); nearly horizontal and laterally projected (1) (Salgado et al. 1997).
rationale: Same orientation of the iliac preacetabular process/lobe from near-vertical to laterally turned/horizontal; the later wording specifies the ventral portion more explicitly.

superseded_definition: Orientation of spinous processes of cranial thoracic vertebrae (U158) / dorsal_or_caudodorsal craniodorsal
retained_definition: Anterior dorsal neural spines inclined posteriorly more than 20 de- gree from vertical: absent (0); present (1) (modified from Wilson and Sereno 1998).
rationale: Both score cranial/anterior dorsal neural-spine orientation. C12 separates craniodorsal inclination from dorsal/caudodorsal, whereas GA11 separates strong posterior inclination from the remaining orientations. The underlying orientation variable is the same.

superseded_definition: Posterior dorsal and/or sacral neural spines, dorsoventral height to centrum length ratio: 2.0 or greater (0); less than 2.0 (2) (Upchurch, 1998; Wilson, 2002; polarity reversed here).
retained_definition: Sacral neural spines, length: approximately twice (0) or four times (1) length of centrum.
rationale: Both derive from the Wilson/Upchurch neural-spine-height lineage and measure neural-spine height relative to centrum length. M19/M26 broaden the serial scope from sacrals to posterior dorsals and/or sacrals and repartition the threshold states.

superseded_definition: Anteriormost caudal centra, lowest average Elongation Index [aEI; centrum anteroposterior length (excluding articular ball) divided by the mean average value of the anterior surface mediolateral width and dorsoventral height] value of: less than 0.6 (0); 0.6 or greater (1) (Gauthier, 1986; Upchurch, 1995, 1998; Upchurch et al., 2004; Mannion et al., 2013; revised here to only include the anteriormost caudal vertebrae).
retained_definition: Ratio of proximodistal length:dorsoventral height of proximal caudal vertebral body (U177) / '>=0.6' '<0.6'
rationale: Both quantify elongation of the proximal/anteriormost caudal centrum. C12 uses length:dorsoventral-height; M19/M26 use average elongation index with mean width/height in the denominator and restrict scoring to the anteriormost caudals.

superseded_definition: Middle caudal centra, average Elongation Index [aEI; centrum anteroposterior length (excluding articular ball) divided by the mean average value of the anterior surface mediolateral width and dorsoven- tral height (excluding chevron facets)] value: less than 1.4 (0); 1.4 or higher (1) (Upchurch & Martin, 2003; Upchurch et al., 2004; Whitlock, 2011a; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Ratio of vertebral body length:height in middle caudal vertebrae (U179) / '<2.0' '>=2.0'
rationale: Both quantify middle-caudal centrum elongation. C12 uses length:height; M19/M26 use average elongation index and a different threshold.

superseded_definition: Metacarpals, metacarpal IV has a prominent proximolateral projection that wraps around the dorsal (anterior) face of metacarpal V (metacarpal IV often forms a chevron shape in proximal end view): absent (0); present (1) (D’Emic, 2012; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Metacarpal IV, articulation for metacarpal V, shape: anteroposteriorly long, broad articular surface (0); articular surface forms a near right angle, transverse and anteroposterior dimen- sions of proximal end subequal (1).
rationale: M19/M26 explicitly cite D'Emic (2012) for the metacarpal-IV/V articulation. DE12 describes the facet geometry; the later formulation operationalizes the derived morphology as a proximolateral projection of metacarpal IV wrapping onto metacarpal V.

superseded_definition: Astragalus, posterior margin bears a tongue- like projection posteromedial to the ascending process, which is separated from the latter by a groove: present (0); absent (1) (D’Emic, 2012; Mannion et al., 2013).
retained_definition: Astragalus, posterior end of proximal face, tubercle: present (0); absent (1).
rationale: M19/M26 explicitly cite D'Emic (2012) for this posterior astragalar projection. The DE12 'tubercle' and later tongue-like posteromedial projection are treated as successive formulations of the same anatomical character.
